strategy.action_description: Replace the GEMM2 serial per-thread I-loop with a qwen_tp2-specialized warp-sliced K/I dequant dot. For each active local slot and hidden column, assign one warp to the output, let lanes own disjoint 32-element scale blocks of I=1024, load mid activations and packed FP4 weights with the existing vectorized/cache-policy helpers, accumulate lane-local FP32 partials, then warp-reduce to the same finalize path used by the parent. Keep scheduling, GEMM1, router weighting, and the parent two-column/fallback code unchanged; the category under test is GEMM2 tiled FP4 dequant work partitioning.
strategy.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: 83d98be7 passed at 566.304 us, slower than 6ebb0ad6 but correctness-clean. Code evidence in 83d98be7 shows GEMM2 added adjacent-H two-column reuse, yet each participating thread still walks all gemm2_scale_cols for I=1024 serially inside accumulate_fp4_pair_scaled_i_tiles_gemm2. Prior lineage evidence: GEMM1 warp-sliced K dequant in 06419529 was the first large stable improvement, whereas prior GEMM2 H-tiling and two-column attempts did not split K across lanes. New L1 evidence: the local SM120 NVFP4 split-K/GEMV reports identify small-M long-K work as a parallelism problem, use K-splitting when the serial dot under-fills or has long instruction chains, and require alignment predicates; the vectorized-loads card recommends many lanes per row/dot with 128-bit or wider FP4 loads and cache-policy separation. Inference: GEMM2 still has a serial software-FP4 dequant chain per output. Action: apply the successful warp-sliced K idea to GEMM2 instead of adding more H-column reuse.
strategy.expected_impact: Should shorten the per-thread dequant/FMA chain in GEMM2, improve instruction-level and memory-level parallelism across I scale blocks, and preserve the parent finalization semantics. It is most likely to help when GEMM2 remains visible after GEMM1 warp-slicing.
strategy.risks: One warp per output increases warp count and shuffle overhead, and may be slower if launch occupancy rather than serial K latency is the limit. Restrict the fast path to I_scale_vec==32 and I_scale_cols==32, keep the parent serial/two-column path as fallback, and watch register pressure from per-lane accumulators.
